scope: Twenty-one remaining specimen source bodies and bounded seven-parent/fourteen-native context, not a repeated exhaustive ordinary-lesson audit. Source-first within this phase with earlier project/pathology knowledge known; not blind independent acceptance.

units.requirement: A core preserves some local tissue relationships while representing only selected positions and finite material, rather than the whole target.
Image targeting, sample acquisition, represented interfaces and preservation are distinct: a core does not guarantee the relevant interface or every tumour population was sampled.
Prepared sections provide morphology and contextual architecture; collection from a living tumour does not itself create a viable-cell bank or a named molecular result.

Technical readability and radiology–pathology concordance are separate. In the fictional suspicious target/benign-fat example, preservation does not prove the target benign or prescribe a follow-up procedure.

Retain named site, block/region, preservation, intended assay and tissue use. Core length/count is inventory, not tumour content or a universal adequacy rule; diagnostic adequacy may differ from another assay.
No tumour seen refers to submitted material in sampling context; a core alone does not establish whole-lesion composition, complete surgical margins or individual treatment benefit.
The later-only NRG-BR005 context reports 50-percent sensitivity in 101 evaluable women after neoadjuvant therapy; the population, reference surgery and limited sampling must stay attached.

The native strip, enlarged clipped core and wider target are fictional drawing geometry. Preserve the same selected window across depictions without treating its colours, shapes or sampled fraction as empirical data.
FNA recovers cells and fluid and can include clusters and small tissue fragments; it is not exclusively dispersed single cells or an information-free alternative to a core.
Cytology examines recovered cell shapes, nuclei and groupings; cellular evidence and original tissue architecture answer different questions.
A suitable cell block can support sectioning and additional staining or molecular tests, but it does not reconstruct the original lesion map or guarantee every ancillary test.
Finding malignant cells can be useful in context without establishing the full breast duct-boundary/invasion relationship, lesion extent or every lymph node.
Adequacy, a negative result and an inadequate result are distinct; rapid assessment can inform adequacy without guaranteeing downstream success or representativeness.

Retain site, preparation, relevant cellularity, intended question and validation. Blood dilution, preservation, missed target and finite sample can limit findings; one retrospective breast cohort is not universal performance.

The fictional malignant-cell exercise does not establish exact invasive extent. Conditional cell-block symbols are not a measured recovery fraction or a guarantee that every represented cell survives.
An archived specimen is finite. Sections leave the block, extraction uses material and disrupts its original architecture, and different depths can contain different mixtures.
Stored slides/data and digital copying are distinct from replacing physical tissue: reanalysis or copies do not refill the block, and creating the original image used prepared material.

An aliquot is an allocated portion. Retain site/date/treatment, preservation, position, amount, previous use and remaining suitable material; a block or slide count does not establish relevant-cell adequacy.
Diagnostic needs, optional assays, question/input fit, research permission and institutional custody are separate allocation considerations; biological suitability is not automatic availability.

There is no universal allocation fraction, section thickness, number of tests or core/slide count that proves adequacy. Inventory exhaustion, wrong region and duplicate destructive work are different failure modes.

A new biopsy is a new procedure and time point, while an expanded culture is a changed system. Neither recreates the exact archived original; the fictional overlapping-RNA requests require coordination rather than a personal allocation rule.
FFPE chemical stabilization and wax sections preserve architectural information and can support assays validated for that input; fixed material is not universally unusable for molecular testing.
The Masuda fixation experiment supports altered RNA chemistry and assay behaviour at its experimental scope, without a modern clinical performance estimate.

Fresh-frozen is a preparation history, not proof of viable recovery. The cited NCI molecular snap-freezing protocol expressly excludes viability, sorting, culture and drug-sensitivity applications from its scope.
Viable-cell work requires actual recovery, relevant identity, function and assay/model fit. A viable label does not guarantee a useful culture or individual drug-response prediction.
Designed cryopreservation may support recovery, while extraction of measurable molecules from fixed tissue does not restore its original living cells. No universal best preparation follows.
Preparation categories do not identify tumour content or whole-lesion representation; retain aliquot site, collection time, treatment context and represented cells.

Assay-specific quality, quantity, stabilization, fixative compatibility, degradation and thaw recovery are distinct checks. Validation on fixed tissue does not transfer automatically to frozen or cultured material.
In the fictional fixed/frozen/viable archive, no label alone proves the growth experiment possible. Preparation is chosen for the question and finite allocation rather than ranked universally.
A resection specimen needs site, procedure, clinical context, documented orientation and sampled-region identities; deformable tissue is not a rigid reconstruction of the body.
Sutures, clips, marks and ink colours require a recorded local key; no unfamiliar stitch or colour has universal anatomical meaning.

Marked surfaces and sampled microscopic margins are interpreted with handling context. Ink entering cracks, fragmentation or uncertain orientation can mislead; a drawn boundary alone is not a margin result or clearance claim.
Gross features/dimensions and selected cassette/block sections are mapped to the specimen. Large size or many slides does not establish cell-by-cell whole-specimen examination.
A molecular result from central block A cannot be assigned to block B, a different surface or an unsampled margin merely because they came from the same operation.

Treatment timing, site and preservation constrain the biological time point. Allocation must retain diagnostic mapping and location; post-treatment resection and pretreatment biopsy are not interchangeable.

Retain specimen parts, block map, applicable dimensions/distances/units and reporting context. Gross specimen size is not automatically invasive tumour size; examined margins/nodes do not settle all unsampled disease or individual recurrence risk.
RNA extraction loses tissue context. Integrity/fragmentation and chemical damage are different from quantity; a large yield can still be unsuitable.
An electropherogram characterizes size-associated signal and multiple trace features; its schematic early/18S/28S pattern is not a transcript-by-transcript integrity assay.
RIN is a multi-feature method-defined 1-to-10 scale from degraded to intact. It is not percent intact messenger RNA, viable cells, tumour purity or a computed score for the invented trace.
DV200 concerns the measured size fraction above 200 nucleotides under actual smear-region/marker rules. It is not transcript-specific integrity, a universal pass cutoff or guaranteed assay success.

In the invented 0-to-600-nt equal-width 100-nt histogram, heights [1,3,2,2,1,1] yield selected area above 200 of 6/10=60 percent, separate from the RIN trace. This is not a literal molecule-count distribution or imported source data.
The older fixed-ovarian-tumour study evaluates shorter-fragment metrics and downstream library performance in its own protocol; its RIN/DV200 limitations are not a universal modern assay ranking.

Short-target recovery and full-length transcript/splice evidence are different. The fictional low-RIN sample can fit one validated expression workflow and not another; a negative result may reflect failed recovery rather than biological absence.
Passing input quality checks does not establish library complexity or gene recovery. Preservation, chemical modifications, contaminants, amount and downstream assay controls remain distinct.

Retain preservation, aliquot/tissue cost, exact question/method, RIN scale, fragment metric, RNA amount in ng and downstream metrics. Laboratory acceptance criteria and diagnostic validation remain assay-specific.
Vacuum assistance acquires multiple tissue pieces through a positioned probe using suction/cutting; it does not itself identify malignancy or measure a molecular biomarker.

Several recovered pieces can broaden sampled material while retaining selected positions and heterogeneous composition; there is no universal piece count proving adequacy or whole-target representation.

Separate pieces differ from a documented oriented excision and mapped outer surface. The native contrast and local handling/ink caveats are not a universal rule for all margin assessment or proof of complete removal.
Pathological examination and correspondence to the imaging target, including a calcification-defined target when relevant, are distinct from simply seeing less abnormality afterward.
Collection technique and preservation are separate; vacuum-collected formalin-fixed material is not a living-cell bank merely because of the collection method.

Retain named site, inventory, preparation, represented cells and intended assay. Bleeding, damage, necrosis, missed target and insufficient analyte are distinct limits; each ancillary assay has its own input/validation requirements.

In the fictional sampled-pieces/imaging exercise, consistent pieces and little visible abnormality do not prove all microscopic disease gone or negative surgical margins. The three selected windows and inked outline are invented.

The original RESPONDER context describes 398 women with imaging response, all subtypes, biopsy followed by standard surgery; that denominator/design remains distinct from the residual-cancer subgroup.
Both versions retain RESPONDER residual cancer missed in 37 of 208 women whose surgery found it, giving a false-negative rate of 17.8 percent under that protocol, not a universal biopsy rate.
The original-only RESPONDER 6.2-percent result combines imaging with biopsy in an exploratory analysis; it is not the main result or a validated universal decision rule.

The original-only Kuerer cohort is a single-arm phase 2 selection of 50 women aged at least 40 with TNBC or HER2-positive cancer, residual lesion under 2 cm and at least 12 cores; those conditions constrain interpretation.

The original-only Kuerer report has 31 biopsy-defined pCR cases, 62 percent, receiving radiotherapy without breast surgery and no in-breast recurrences at median 26.4 months. This finite selected follow-up is not a universal safety guarantee.

A biopsy-defined response samples the bed. Trial design, selection, imaging and reference surgery or follow-up limit generalization; the lesson route to comparison trials does not itself establish a current surgical policy.
All 21 assigned bodies were read from byte zero to end at the original pin; exact identity supports later reuse while both 42 version entries remain.
All seven eligible later parent bodies and full original-to-later differences were read after frontmatter/generated-navigation/personal-case gates; no ordinary grade is replaced.
Fourteen whole native variants and complete selected index rows were viewed/read; associated SHA/Git identities and sourceSections establish identity, not semantic or clinical acceptance.
Historical PASS/REVISE and prospective/not-adopted states retain dates and scope. Original creators, reuse authors, task authors, reviewers and root integrators are distinct roles.
Private source/capture paths, generator dependency promises and historical source commits are not followed or fetched. Stage/preimage/prospective/pinned hashes are not conflated.
Alt/caption/handling text duplicated in provenance receives no duplicate science credit. Pending provenance may precede a later review; same-size different-hash stages remain distinct.
Inherited abstract/selected-source/native claims are not fresh reads. Any reused earlier assessment needs exact capture identity and its original depth; no whole-paper claim is inferred.
RIN bins, sampled patches, ink keys, shapes and physical/data arrows are authored conventions. FNA short edge strokes are not a stray text token merely because they resemble a letter.

Mermaid source reading is separate from rendered review. Native Sharp/vips views do not establish browser/hydration/mobile, numerical contrast, focus trap, expert or accessibility acceptance; BODY focus/Tab-escape findings stay open.
No main/live, independent, expert, owner, learner or language acceptance follows. Protected earlier packets, artwork/ordinary grades and source depths remain unchanged except declared new work.
